description: The member reached the $4,900 out-of-pocket maximum before March 2026, and the cover shows $4,900 of $4,900 used. Even so, claim 1's eye exam charges the $35 eye-exam copay, so the year-to-date member share is higher than the out-of-pocket amount the cover shows. Claim 2 (lab tests) is correct. A careful reviewer should conclude the plan should have paid the full approved amount for the eye exam and the member owes nothing for it.

sources.what: MA plans must have an in-network out-of-pocket maximum, track what enrollees pay and tell them when it is reached (paragraph (f)(4))
Once you reach your plan's yearly limit, you pay nothing for covered services for the rest of the year
sources.source: Medicare.gov, Compare Original Medicare & Medicare Advantage, https://www.medicare.gov/basics/get-started-with-medicare/get-more-coverage/your-coverage-options/compare-original-medicare-medicare-advantage

sources.what: Under the in-network maximum rule, once this plan's $4,900 maximum is reached the plan pays the full approved amount for covered in-network services
sources.source: eCFR, 42 CFR 422.100(f)(4), General requirements (in-network maximum out-of-pocket), https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-B/part-422/subpart-C/section-422.100; Medicare.gov, What does Medicare cost? (plan pays 100% after the limit), https://www.medicare.gov/basics/get-started-with-medicare/medicare-basics/what-does-medicare-cost
